longestProse.value: Red Fox reports apple and currant in Sandia Caturra, and honeysuckle and candy in Bourbon examples. Producer organizations such as CECOVASA and village names help distinguish coffees within Puno. Listed varieties follow Red Fox’s Puno sourcing, separate from CECOVASA’s combined Puno–Cusco list.

The official profile emphasizes distinct acidity and balanced body. Citric acidity, chocolate and cane-sugar sweetness come from UNEX's Acatenango Valley offering; check the growing location alongside the actual processing mill.

Ally Coffee's Las Brisas Kenia Honey comes through José Alvarado's family micromill, Imperio Rojo. Apple, caramel and red grape are this lot's tasting notes; variety and processing create different expressions within Brunca.

Sucafina's Boqueron Oriente Natural dries smallholders' whole cherries on patios. Its berry and hibiscus notes illustrate a processing-specific expression alongside the official region's chocolate descriptor.

The Guji Shakiso washed example uses submerged fermentation followed by drying on shaded raised beds. Its cane-sugar sweetness and juicy character describe that station lot, offering a comparison within Guji.

An origin with producing localities such as Othaya and Karatina and their cooperative factories. Café Imports’ 2020 regional selections combine caramel, white grape, plum and raspberry with lively acidity.

Melbourne Coffee Merchants' Kimbo Estate AA is a washed lot from Lucy Wanjiru's family. The family processes its harvest at its own wet mill; the floral, apple and sugar notes describe this particular lot.

FNC’s region table describes medium citric acidity, while its designation profile says high acidity. Check individual lots. Variety and process follow a Buesaco smallholder washed lot arriving in 2023.
Primavera's La Pila & Neighbours combined 28 smallholders in Santa Ana La Montaña. Its washed coffee, with an additional soaking stage, provides the almond and chocolate tasting example shown here.
Father Coffee's washed Geisha lot 68 from Hartmann in Santa Clara provides the jasmine, white peach and yuzu example. These notes describe a named farm lot rather than all Renacimiento production.
Atlas Coffee Importers describes wet-processed Balinese coffees with bright acidity, soft body, citrus and brown sugar. Farmer-group and processing details help distinguish individual lots.
Named-village and drying-station naturals, such as Banko Gotiti, provide more specific traceability. Distinguish regional selections from individual station lots when recording the origin.
A locality within the Kayanza coffee-trade origin, with Gakenke washing station and its supplying farms. The Gakenke washed lot shows black tea, berries, caramelized sweetness and florals.
Mountain farms produce pulped natural and washed coffees. Cecafes in Venda Nova do Imigrante supports sensory evaluation, processing research and producer training for Arabica and Conilon.
Qima supplies the regional environment and tasting notes; the Louver offering separately supplies variety and processing evidence. The two offerings are not assumed to be the same lot.

Short geographic, variety and flavor terms are factual identifiers and no infringement inference was made from their overlap.

contentReview.conclusion: No reproduced long source paragraphs or source images found in inspected public origin rendering path. Broad legal permission for systematic data reuse must be assessed separately.
